title: Opening of the Tokaido Shinkansen
summary: On 1 October 1964 the Tokaido Shinkansen began service between Tokyo and Osaka, nine days before the opening ceremony of the Tokyo Olympics. The Diet had approved the plan in March 1959 to relieve capacity shortages on the Tokaido corridor. The new 515 km line is described as the world's first high-speed rail service.

as_recorded.value: On the 1st of October, 1964, the inaugural service of the Shinkansen began with much fanfare.

where.modern_name: Tokyo, Japan (western terminus; the line ran to Osaka)
where.historical_name: Tokyo, Japan (Japanese National Railways line between Tokyo and Osaka)

importance.justification: The first high-speed rail line, which set the model for fast intercity rail around the world.
